name: Undersea cables & GPS
summary: Finnish court case over Baltic cable damage concludes; GPS jamming persists on NATO's eastern flank
state: A Helsinki court has heard the case against the captain and boatswain of the Fitburg over cable damage in the Gulf of Finland on 31 Dec, and Yle reported a conviction for aggravated sabotage on 5 Nov; it can be appealed (Yle; Maritime Executive). GPS interference continues along NATO's eastern flank. The ruling concerns a past incident and no new cable cut was reported as of 7 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Airline passengers are not at risk from GPS jamming; pilots use backup navigation.
rubric_hit: Cable damage case and widespread GNSS interference = Watch

sources.title: Maritime Executive — Captain and boatswain go on trial in Finland

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
